meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and, but; so', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'to you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?
And this is for you. A toy car!

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'what', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning '(emphasis) after all, but', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

Prefix 'пред-' ('before, fore-') indicates anticipation or prior position (stem 'упредить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to warn, notify in advance', paired with 'предупреждать'.

examples.trans: And they warned me very strictly!

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('necessary, needed').
Prefix 'об-' ('around, about') marks encirclement or comprehensive action (stem 'язательно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Государство обязательно увидит и назначит операцию.
examples.trans: The state will surely see and will schedule the surgery.
I'll definitely buy you a tank.

meanings.note: Prefix 'пред-' ('before, fore-') indicates anticipation or prior position (stem 'упреждать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to warn', paired with 'предупредить'.

examples.trans: I am warning you for the last time.

examples.text: О чём предупреждал? Да ты что делаешь?
examples.trans: Warned me about what? Hey, what are you doing?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'yes, indeed', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'no; there isn't', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('new').

examples.text: Ну что, довольна? Теперь новую работу искать.
examples.trans: Well, happy now? Now I have to look for a new job.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'aquarium' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Это что ещё за стеклянный аквариум?
examples.trans: What kind of glass aquarium is this?

зайти.gloss: to come in, to drop in

meanings.en: to come in, to drop in
meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to come in, to drop in', paired with 'заходить'.

examples.trans: I'll drop by in the evening.

examples.text: Ну, как хочешь. Лидия Алексеевна, зайдите, пожалуйста!
examples.trans: Well, as you like. Lidia Alekseyevna, come in, please!

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'party' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Приводи её сегодня к Димону на вечеринку!
examples.trans: Bring her to Dimon's party tonight!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'but', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо ещё.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need more.
I want to, but I can't.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'how; as', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'well; come on', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'all right, OK', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: All right, here you go. There, look.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'let', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Ты преподавай. А они пусть строят свои торговые центры.
examples.trans: You teach. And let them build their shopping centres.

examples.text: А они пусть строят свои торговые центры.
examples.trans: And let them build their shopping centres.

meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'езжать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to come (by transport), to arrive', paired with 'приехать'.
High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'she; it', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Паша, я больше не хочу о ней слышать. Понял?
examples.trans: Pasha, I don't want to hear about her again. Understood?

просить.gloss: to ask, to request, to beg

meanings.en: to ask, to request, to beg
meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'сить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to ask, to request, to beg', paired with 'попросить'.

examples.text: Когда вырасту, ты будешь просить у меня прощения!
examples.trans: When I grow up, you'll be begging me to forgive you!

examples.text: Аракелян просит время. Сумма очень большая.
examples.trans: Arakelyan is asking for more time. The sum is very large.
Samsonov, I asked you not to!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'so that, in order to', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I'm calling to say thank you.
So that there are witnesses, Samson.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'we', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

подъехать.gloss: to drive up, arrive by car

meanings.en: to drive up, arrive by car
meanings.note: Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'ъехать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to drive up, arrive by car'.

related.gloss: not to to drive up (negated infinitive)

examples.trans: I can drive over there too!

examples.text: Такси уже подъехало к нашему дому.
examples.trans: The taxi has already driven up to our house.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'at, by; (у меня) I have', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'овершенно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Совершенно верно, я мэр этого города.
examples.trans: Quite right, I am the mayor of this town.
This is a completely new car.

examples.text: Совершенно верно, я мэр этого города. И предложение у меня к вам такое.
examples.trans: Quite right, I am the mayor of this town. And my offer to you is this.

meanings.note: Common neuter noun meaning 'time' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Я и сама хорошо проведу время.
examples.trans: I'll have a good time on my own.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'there', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'everything, all; that's it', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Мы просто не хотели вас беспокоить. Всё отменим!
examples.trans: We just didn't want to bother you. We'll cancel it all!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'then, later, afterwards', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'I', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
